evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: Prevents concept controls from being mistaken for production evidence and makes promotion contingent on canonical ownership and executable wiring evidence.
items.statement: The inventory repeatedly and explicitly classifies owner-adjudicated controls as source-lineage only, not production evidence, until an owner document accepts behavior and command, state, receipt, and test wiring exists.
items.title: Concept-lineage authority boundary is explicit

items.impact: Mute and Focus context-lens choices cannot be treated as accessible production interactions without roles, keyboard activation, focus semantics, and regression evidence.
items.statement: Interactive context-lens custom elements are explicitly recorded with missing semantic roles and no keyboard parity.
items.title: Context-lens custom controls are not keyboard accessible

items.impact: A production rendering could display an indefinite Compacting state with no command dispatch, completion, error, retry, cancellation, or receipt oracle.
items.statement: Compact Now only mutates its label and opacity while the control has no canonical command, leaving the real lifecycle and failure recovery undefined.
items.title: Compact Now has only a visual pending state

items.impact: The concept communicates intended context behavior, but selection scope, persistence, conflicts, summary provenance, and off-state restoration remain owner decisions.
items.statement: Context Lens presents Focus, Subcompact, and Turn Off behavior, including replacing content with a local summary, but does not promote those interactions into a production contract.
items.title: Context Lens mode behavior is concept-only

items.impact: Promotion without an archive authority, confirmation policy, idempotency, concurrent-state handling, undo or restore semantics, and receipts could cause silent thread loss or misleading success.
items.statement: Thread Archive controls are visible but have no handler or production command contract.
items.title: Archive is an unwired destructive action

evidence.exact_quote: "label": "4m Test Suite Parallelization 25 subagents: 8 done, 11 running, 2 failed ~2 min remaining",

items.impact: If promoted directly, counts, failure states, and remaining-time claims could be stale or internally inconsistent under concurrent fan-out, retries, cancellation, or partial telemetry loss.
items.statement: Thread rows expose detailed live-looking orchestration status but do not bind those labels to authoritative state, event ordering, receipts, refresh rules, or falsifiable timing or count invariants.
items.title: Operational thread status lacks a truth contract

items.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot reliably identify or activate thread switching, and production tests need semantic activation parity rather than DOM-click evidence.
items.statement: Clickable thread rows are recorded as custom targets without roles and without keyboard parity.
items.title: Thread switching is pointer-only

evidence.exact_quote: "label": "1h Refactor Database Layer Consolidated queries into repository pattern. Ran `cargo test`, 35 passed.",

"owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: A test-pass label can imply executable certification despite the inventory's own lineage-only status; production GUI truth must derive from receipts linked to the exact run and revision.
items.statement: The concept displays a concrete `cargo test` success count, but no run identity, revision, receipt, freshness, or failure-to-refresh behavior makes that claim production-verifiable.
items.title: Test success text is not receipt-backed

items.impact: Even rows without inline handlers remain visually action-like and need a defined semantic role, focus model, and non-pointer selection contract if promoted.
items.statement: Thread-style rows in this window are explicitly identified as custom click targets lacking semantic roles.
items.title: Thread rows lack accessible semantics

evidence.exact_quote: "label": "1d FileSafe Blocking Addressed write block on config.json. User explicitly allowed YOLO bypass.",
"label": "2d PRD Builder Generated PRD draft. Awaiting Approve And Build.",

items.impact: A production UI could falsely imply that write protections were knowingly bypassed or that a build is safely awaiting approval without proving actor, scope, expiry, target revision, or the exact authorized side effects.
items.statement: Authority-sensitive claims about a YOLO write bypass and Approve And Build are displayed as thread status without a canonical authority or approval receipt contract.
items.title: Bypass and build-approval status are not authority-bound

evidence.exact_quote: "Production-looking control needs a concrete UICommand or explicit retirement before implementation.",
"No production command is assigned in this repair; remains concept lineage until an owner doc promotes it and adds command/state/handler/receipt/test evidence.",

items.impact: The explicit gate blocks implementation certification from relying on production-looking concept controls until owner promotion supplies complete executable evidence.
items.statement: The reconciliation explicitly requires either a concrete UICommand or retirement and says command, state, handler, receipt, and test evidence must precede promotion.
items.title: Production-looking controls have an explicit promotion gate

items.impact: The active browser-testing thread cannot be certified for keyboard or assistive-technology navigation from this concept control.
items.statement: The browser-testing thread switcher is a custom clickable target with no role and no keyboard parity.
items.title: Browser-testing thread activation is inaccessible

items.impact: Draft persistence, submit idempotency, interrupt races, edit/resend lineage, cancel recovery, and concurrent task state could diverge or lose user intent without explicit command and receipt contracts.
items.statement: Save Draft, Submit, Resend, Edit, Steer (Interrupt), and Cancel are visible message controls but the concept entries do not define production handlers, state transitions, failure outcomes, or receipts.
items.title: Message mutation and interruption lifecycle is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: "test_evidence": "production render/control, dispatcher, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence required before implementation certification"

items.impact: The contract sharply separates file restoration from conversational rewind and blocks certification until render, dispatch, disabled reason, receipt or event, accessibility, and regression evidence exists.
items.statement: Revert Last Edit has a canonical command, handler, enabled and disabled selectors, receipt or event effect, accessibility contract, and explicit implementation-certification evidence gate.
items.title: Revert Last Edit has a bounded production wiring contract

evidence.exact_quote: "title": "cmd.chat.rewind \u2014 Conversation history only. Does NOT restore files.",
"test_evidence": "production render/control, dispatcher, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence required before implementation certification"

items.impact: Users are explicitly protected from mistaking chat rewind for file rollback, and certification is tied to executable evidence.
items.statement: Rewind Chat explicitly affects conversation history only, leaves files unchanged, and has a canonical command and evidence-gated wiring contract.
items.title: Rewind Chat is explicitly separated from file restoration

items.impact: Auto-approval can authorize consequential tools; without scope, actor, expiry, per-tool policy, confirmation overrides, audit receipts, revocation, and accessible state, a UI toggle could silently broaden authority.
items.statement: YOLO is described as Auto-approve tools but is only a class-toggle concept control with no canonical command or authority contract.
items.title: YOLO auto-approval is authority-sensitive and unwired

items.impact: Production attachment handling needs path normalization, permission and size checks, privacy scope, upload or snapshot timing, offline behavior, removal semantics, undo, stale-reference detection, and send-time receipts.
items.statement: The concept exposes file attachment chips and removes them directly from the DOM, without a production data-lifecycle or untrusted-input contract.
items.title: Attachment chips lack a data-lifecycle contract

items.impact: The GUI can suggest a selected provider model and reasoning level without defining availability, entitlement, fallback, persistence, per-message versus per-thread scope, cost disclosure, or receipt projection.
items.statement: Model and effort selectors expose concrete values but only toggle dropdown visibility; the selection, validation, fallback, and state-source contracts are absent from these concept controls.
items.title: Model and effort selectors lack authoritative state

evidence.exact_quote: "Contains mock/demo/local fixture state and is excluded from acceptance evidence unless replaced by a real state contract."

items.impact: The fixture boundary prevents demo terminal interactions from satisfying production acceptance until a real state contract replaces them.
items.statement: Terminal demo controls are explicitly marked concept_fixture_only and excluded from acceptance evidence unless replaced by real state contracts.
items.title: Terminal demo controls are excluded from acceptance evidence

items.impact: A command-looking token in a demo can be mistaken for implemented routing; production renderers and tests must not infer command availability from fixture tokens.
items.statement: Open and Show Terminal expose `cmd.terminal.show` tokens while remaining fixture-only and lacking a canonical command binding in these entries.
items.title: Terminal command tokens are not production wiring

items.impact: Output, Problems, Ports, and information affordances need semantic roles, names, focus-visible states, keyboard activation, and selected-state announcements before production use.
items.statement: Terminal navigation chips and information icons are click-only spans with recorded role and keyboard-parity failures.
items.title: Terminal navigation chips are inaccessible

segments.summary: Reviewed usage, context detail and compaction controls, issue fixture, thread-panel actions, search, and initial Context Lens modes; retained the explicit lineage boundary while identifying visual-only async state and click-only accessibility gaps.

Reviewed Focus and Subcompact mode details, Turn Off, chat-sidebar collapse, fixture thread metadata, and Archive and More controls; mode semantics remain conceptual and archive lacks a destructive-action lifecycle.

Reviewed debug, subagent, crew, migration, and batch-fanout thread rows plus repeated Archive and More actions; live-looking orchestration projections lack truth invariants and clickable rows lack semantic keyboard access.

Reviewed blocked-agent, document, test-result, bug-fix, research-decision, and repeated thread actions; concrete success labels are not receipt-backed and action-like rows remain semantically inaccessible.

Reviewed Context Lens, FileSafe YOLO-bypass, PRD Builder, browser-testing, Archive and More, Copy, and Edit controls; high-risk authority claims lack receipts, while the source correctly blocks production promotion absent UICommand and full wiring evidence.

Reviewed message Copy, Edit, Resend, questionnaire, Dismiss, Save Draft, Submit, Steer, Cancel, overflow reveal, and Revert Last Edit; generic mutation actions lack lifecycles, while Revert has a bounded evidence-gated production contract.

Reviewed Rewind Chat, file-reference chips, composer, attachments, agent and persona selectors, ELI5, YOLO, CREW, and Stop; Rewind is correctly scoped, while auto-approval authority and attachment lifecycle remain unspecified.

Reviewed model and effort selectors, document Copy and information controls, terminal show, focus, transcript, Output, Problems, Ports, and related fixtures; fixture exclusion is explicit, but selector truth, command-token seams, and click-only terminal navigation remain gaps.
